paras: The Benton burglary suspect mock hanging was an episode in late May 1882 in which a number of citizens at Benton, Minnesota, put a rope around the neck of a man suspected of burglary and marched him to a tree to force a confession. The man was not hanged; after he confessed he was arrested. The episode is known from a single brief item in a column of state news.

According to the New Ulm Weekly Review, the man, whose name was not given, was suspected of a burglary at Benton and was taken "a few days" before the paper's issue of May 31, 1882, by "a number of citizens." His captors put a rope around his neck, marched him to a tree and "extorted from him a confession." Upon this, the paper said, he was "duly arrested"; the item does not say where he was held or what he had confessed to.
The item reports no arrest or prosecution of the citizens who seized him, and no report of a trial of the suspect was found.

The New Ulm Weekly Review ran the story as one sentence in its "Minnesota News" column, between an item on a frost at Rochester and one on tramps robbing a hotel in Shakopee. It offered no comment, though its wording called the confession "extorted" and the arrest "duly" made. The item names neither the suspect nor his race, and gives no county for Benton.
